title: L.A.M.B.

{{Short description|Fashion line}} {{About|the fashion line by Gwen Stefani|Stefani's album|Love. Angel. Music. Baby.|other uses|Lamb (disambiguation){{!}}Lamb}} {{Use mdy dates|date=June 2024}} {{Infobox company | name = L.A.M.B. | logo = [[Image:L.A.M.B Gwen Stefani.jpg|220px|L.A.M.B. logo]] | type = [[Corporation]] | foundation = 2003 | location = United States | key_people = [[Gwen Stefani]] | industry = [[Consumer goods]] | products = {{Unbulleted list| [[Apparel]]|[[Eyewear]]|[[Fragrances]]|[[Handbags]]|[[Shoes]]|[[Watches]]}} }} '''L.A.M.B.''' is a fashion line by American singer [[Gwen Stefani]], the lead vocalist of the [[rock music|rock]] band [[No Doubt]]. The line manufactures [[Clothing|apparel]] and [[Fashion accessory|fashion accessories]]. It was founded in 2003 and made its runway debut in 2004. The line's name is an [[acronym]] of Stefani's debut solo album ''[[Love. Angel. Music. Baby.]]'' As of 2015, the line currently focuses on [[eyewear]].{{cite web | title=Gwen Stefani Reflects on 15 Years as a Fashion Designer: "Music or Fashion, It's Emotional" | website=The Hollywood Reporter | date=2019-02-08 | url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lifestyle/style/gwen-stefani-reflects-15-years-as-a-fashion-designer-1182632/ | access-date=2023-08-11}} The line was influenced by a variety of cultures' fashions, including [[Guatemala]]n, [[Japan]]ese, [[India]]n and [[Jamaica]]n styles. Stefani came from a family of [[seamstress]]es. This further inspired her to launch her own fashion line. The line achieved popularity among celebrities and was worn by stars such as [[Teri Hatcher]], [[Nicole Kidman]], [[Paris Hilton]] and Stefani herself. The fashion line made a runway debut in the spring collection of 2004Van Meter, Jonathan [http://www.style.com/vogue/feature/032204/page2.html "The First Lady of Rock"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080120225434/http://www.style.com/vogue/feature/032204/page2.html |date=2008-01-20 }}''[[Vogue (magazine)|Vogue]]'', retrieved October 12, 2007 and achieved mainstream success at [[New York Fashion Week]] in 2005. An additional fashion line, called [[Harajuku Lovers]], was subsequently launched by Stefani. ==History== Stefani's first experience designing clothes came when she and her mother would sew clothes for themselves when she was young. Stefani comes from a long line of seamstresses, as even her great-grandmother would sew clothes. Stefani made most of the things she wore onstage during concerts. When she became successful and began to tour constantly, she felt she lost her way. Then she met the stylist [[Andrea Lieberman]]. Lieberman introduced her to [[ready-to-wear]] clothing. Later Lieberman became her creative consultant and [[Zaldy Goco]] took over as the head designer.[http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/61621/stefanis-little-lamb-hitting-big-time "Billboard News"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141002011838/http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/61621/stefanis-little-lamb-hitting-big-time |date=2014-10-02 }} ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' Retrieved January 28, 2017 Goco parted ways with L.A.M.B. in 2007.{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/09/07/fashion/zaldy-onetime-club-kid-model-and-costumer-to-pop-stars-returns-to-fashion-week.html |title=Another Life in the Many Lives of Zaldy |first=William |last=Van Meter |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=2014-09-05 |access-date=2024-06-02}} L.A.M.B. started out as a collaboration with [[LeSportsac]] in 2003. The name L.A.M.B. is an acronym which stands for ''Love. Angel. Music. Baby.'', which is also the name of Stefani's first solo album. ==Products== [[File:L.A.M.B. wedge heel.jpg|thumb|A L.A.M.B. label wedge-heel shoe]] The fashion line manufactures clothes, shoes, bags and a fragrance called "L". The brand started out as a line for women but claims the track items are unisex. The clothes were manufactured by Ska Girl LLC, which was founded in 2003 by Ken Erman, president of L.A.M.B. The eyewear collection launched in January 2016. It won 3 of 20/20 - Vision Monday Reader's Choice awards: Frame Brand Introduced 2016, Sunglass Brand Introduced 2016 & Frame Brand – Women.{{cite web |url=https://www.tura.com/brands/l-a-m-b/l-a-m-b-brand-story |title=L.A.M.B. Brand Story | Tura |access-date=2017-10-31 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107010706/https://www.tura.com/brands/l-a-m-b/l-a-m-b-brand-story |archive-date=2017-11-07 }} L.A.M.B joined with [[Royal Elastics]] for the shoe line. Stefani then started to widen the footwear line for adults to include [[Boot|boots]] and [[stilettos]].[http://www.contactmusic.com/new/xmlfeed.nsf/mndwebpages/stefani%20includes%20baby%20shoes%20in%20lamb%20line_29_04_2006 "Stefani includes Baby Shoes in L.A.M.B line"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080602125620/http://www.contactmusic.com/new/xmlfeed.nsf/mndwebpages/stefani%20includes%20baby%20shoes%20in%20lamb%20line_29_04_2006 |date=June 2, 2008}} ''Contactmusic'' Retrieved October 13, 2007 L.A.M.B collaborated with [[Coty Inc.]] for the fragrance and with LeSportsac for handbags in 2003. Stefani went on to design a new line of handbags with Shifter and Partners in 2006. The bags feature LeSportsac's rip-stop [[nylon]] along with a variety of antiqued metal hardware, leather trims and colorful linings. Stefani planned to design [[lingerie]] as well as make-up products for L.A.M.B. L.A.M.B. partnered with Vestal Group on a line of 39 women's watches.[http://www.licensemag.com/licensemag/article/articleDetail.jsp?id=357466 "Weekly E-News, Issue #169, July 11, 2006"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080605011036/http://www.licensemag.com/licensemag/article/articleDetail.jsp?id=357466 |date=June 5, 2008 }} Licencemag.com Retrieved October 12, 2007 L.A.M.B. products were relatively expensive, with apparel priced $55 to $1100, handbags priced $80 to $825, and watches priced $125 to $995.Marsh, Lisa [http://www.elle.com/TheWeekInFashion/8942/gwen-stefani-june-30-2006.html "Gwen Stefani: June 30, 2006"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080303193806/http://www.elle.com/TheWeekInFashion/8942/gwen-stefani-june-30-2006.html |date=March 3, 2008 }} ''[[Elle (magazine)|Elle]]'' Retrieved November 8, 2007 ===Fragrance=== Coty Inc. announced a global licensing agreement with Stefani, to develop and market [[perfume|fragrances]] for L.A.M.B.[http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/living/fashion/s_483192.html "Briefs: Stefani adds perfume to L.A.M.B. offerings"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071114022650/http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/living/fashion/s_483192.html |date=2007-11-14 }} ''Pittsburgh Tribune'' Retrieved October 13, 2007 The fragrance called "L" was launched in September 2007 at Soho House in [[New York City]]. Stefani worked with perfumer Harry Fremont to develop the scent. Stefani described the fragrance as "it's another thing you can wear and another thing I can be part of creatively. I created it for myself -- it's like me shrunk into a box."Flanagan, Noreen [http://www.ellecanada.com/Beauty/face/splash-dance-gwen-stefani-s-new-fragrance-n239255p1.html "Elle Canada"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080602191815/http://www.ellecanada.com/Beauty/face/splash-dance-gwen-stefani-s-new-fragrance-n239255p1.html |date=June 2, 2008}} ''[[Elle (magazine)|Elle]] Canada''. Retrieved September 14, 2007 ==Promotion and fashion shows== {| width="20%" cellpadding="3" align="right" style="font-size:85%;border-collapse:collapse; background-color:transparent; border-style:none;" | width="20" valign=top | [[Image:Cquote1.svg|20px]] | align="right" |Just wait 'til you get your little hands on L.A.M.B. |- | | align="right" | | width="20" valign=top | [[Image:cquote2.png|20px]] |- | colspan="3" |
—Stefani's song "[[Harajuku Girls (song)|Harajuku Girls]]"
|} Stefani frequently referred to her clothing line in her music, as one of the brand's promotional strategies.Pytlik, Mark [http://www.pitchforkmedia.com/article/record_review/40049-the-sweet-escape "Review : The Sweet Escape"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071024155530/http://www.pitchforkmedia.com/article/record_review/40049-the-sweet-escape|date=2007-10-24}} ''[[Pitchfork Media]]'' Retrieved October 14, 2007 Stefani refers to her clothing line in her songs "[[Wind It Up (Gwen Stefani song)|Wind It Up]]," "[[Love. Angel. Music. Baby.#Songs|Harajuku Girls]]," and "[[Crash (Gwen Stefani song)|Crash]]" (which even incorporates the brand's slogan, "I want you all over me like L.A.M.B.").[http://www.seeklyrics.com/lyrics/Gwen-Stefani/Crash.html "Crash lyrics] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011131407/http://seeklyrics.com/lyrics/Gwen-Stefani/Crash.html |date=2007-10-11 }} Retrieved October 13, 2007 Stefani is often seen wearing her own designs, especially when making public appearances. A thirty-second commercial directed by [[Sophie Muller]] was also released to promote the brand's fragrance.[http://video.aol.com/video-detail/l-fragrance-commercial-by-gwen-stefani/177687335 "L" Fragrance Commercial by Gwen Stefani] ''[[AOL]]'' Retrieved October 13, 2007 L.A.M.B. had participated in the Spring/Summer 2006, 2007, and 2008 [[New York Fashion Week]]s. Stefani described her first line, which debuted on September 16, 2005, as "a little [[Sound of Music]], some [[Orange County, California|Orange County]] [[Cholo#United States and Mexico|chola]] girl, some [[Rastafari movement|Rasta]], and a bit of [[The Great Gatsby]]."[http://www.style.com/fashionshows/collections/S2006RTW/review/LAMB "L.A.M.B"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071022033233/http://www.style.com/fashionshows/collections/S2006RTW/review/LAMB |date=2007-10-22 }} ''Style.com'' Retrieved October 19, 2007 The highlights of the show were purple cars bouncing using [[hydraulics]] while Stefani's song "[[Wind It Up (Gwen Stefani song)|Wind It Up]]" made its debut as the models walked the runway.[http://www.lambfashionshow.com/ Official "Fashion Show video"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070313135610/http://www.lambfashionshow.com/ |date=2007-03-13 }} Retrieved 23 September 2007 For Spring/Summer 2007, Stefani opted for a presentation rather than a catwalk show.[http://www.style.com/fashionshows/collections/S2007RTW/review/LAMB "L.A.M.B Fashion shows"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011122621/http://www.style.com/fashionshows/collections/S2007RTW/review/LAMB |date=2007-10-11 }} ''Style.com'' Retrieved November 11, 2007 The models, all donning identical blond wigs, wore designs Stefani said were inspired by [[Michelle Pfeiffer]]'s role as Elvira Hancock in the 1983 ''[[Scarface (1983 film)|Scarface]]''. The show included some of Stefani's trademark tracksuits and extensively referenced prints from Guatemala, India, and Japan.Maxwell, Alison; Freydkin, Donna; and Barker, Olivia. [http://blogs.usatoday.com/fashion/2006/09/stefani_tends_t.html "Stefani tends to her L.A.M.B."] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090220235720/http://blogs.usatoday.com/fashion/2006/09/stefani_tends_t.html |date=2009-02-20 }} ''[[USA Today]]''. September 15, 2006. May 30, 2007.Borelli, Laird [http://www.style.com/fashionshows/collections/S2007RTW/review/LAMB "Runway Review L.A.M.B"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011122621/http://www.style.com/fashionshows/collections/S2007RTW/review/LAMB |date=2007-10-11 }} ''Style.com'' Retrieved September 29, 2007 On September 5, 2007, L.A.M.B opened [[New York City|New York]]'s Spring/Summer 2008 Mercedes-Benz Fashion Week. The collection "looked like the sixties as seen by someone who grew up in the eighties" and incorporated influences from Stefani's ska roots.[http://www.style.com/fashionshows/collections/S2008RTW/review/LAMB "L.A.M.B"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011050621/http://www.style.com/fashionshows/collections/S2008RTW/review/LAMB |date=2007-10-11 }} ''Style.com'' Retrieved October 19, 2007 ==Critical reception== The line was mostly well received by critics and Stefani was appreciated for taking fashion seriously even though she is a celebrity. Fern Mallis of [[IMG (company)|IMG]] praised the line and Stefani as well and said, "the L.A.M.B. line is clearly at the top of these lines and is as unique and individual as Gwen herself."[https://www.today.com/popculture/stefani-s-l-m-b-gains-fashion-week-respect-wbna20589285 "Stefani's L.A.M.B. gains Fashion Week respect"] msnbc.com Retrieved September 16, 2007 The shoes were well received by the critics, though considered to be pricey. Desiree Stimpert of [[Dotdash|About.com]] said, " ... these shoes aren't for everyone, but will most definitely appeal to fans of Ms. Stefani's music and fashion - sense."Stimpert, Desiree [http://shoes.about.com/od/celebrityshoes/a/gwen_stefani.htm "L.A.M.B Shoes] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071016030736/http://shoes.about.com/od/celebrityshoes/a/gwen_stefani.htm |date=2007-10-16 }} Retrieved 25 September 2007 Tim Stack of ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' said, "L.A.M.B.'s embellished tracksuits, Rasta-inspired knits, and gaucho-heel combos deliver the edge"Stack, Tim [http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,1111192,00.html "L.A.M.B. Shop"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081013204601/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,1111192,00.html |date=2008-10-13 }} ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' Retrieved October 14, 2007 Nicole Phelps of [[Style.com]] said, "The collection, which looked like the sixties as seen by someone who grew up in the eighties, was altogether more wearable and on trend."Phelps, Nicole [http://www.style.com/fashionshows/collections/S2008RTW/review/LAMB "L.A.M.B Spring 2008 Ready - to - wear"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011050621/http://www.style.com/fashionshows/collections/S2008RTW/review/LAMB |date=2007-10-11 }} ''Style.com'' Retrieved October 18, 2007 Fashion journalist [[Cathy Horyn]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' differed and said, "If ever there was a reason for a pop star to concentrate on her vocal skills, it was Gwen Stefani's fashion meltdown."Horyn, Cathy [https://web.archive.org/web/20080329162049/http://runway.blogs.nytimes.com/2007/09/06/spring-rolls-and-arm-candy/index.html?hp "Spring Rolls and Arm Candy"] ''[[The New York Times]]'' Retrieved October 18, 2007 ==Commercial success== The brand was sold in 275 stores worldwide[http://www.chcmedia.com/forums/index.php?showtopic=5366&mode=linear "L.A.M.B To Make $90 Million By End Of Year"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080605012929/http://www.chcmedia.com/forums/index.php?showtopic=5366&mode=linear |date=2008-06-05 }} Retrieved October 12, 2007 and was seen worn on celebrities including [[Teri Hatcher]], [[Nicole Kidman]], [[Kelly Ripa]], [[Paris Hilton]], and Stefani herself.McGibbon, Rob. [http://www.news.com.au/dailytelegraph/story/0,22049,21706422-5006011,00.html "No natural born popstar"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070519042316/http://www.news.com.au/dailytelegraph/story/0%2C22049%2C21706422-5006011%2C00.html |date=2007-05-19 }}. ''[[The Daily Telegraph (Sydney)|The Daily Telegraph]]''. May 13, 2007. Retrieved June 2, 2007.[[Eliscu, Jenny]]. [https://www.rollingstone.com/news/coverstory/gwen_cuts_loose "Gwen Cuts Loose"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090501150654/http://www.rollingstone.com/news/coverstory/gwen_cuts_loose |date=2009-05-01 }}. ''[[Rolling Stone]]'', issue 966. January 27, 2005. Retrieved April 17, 2005. L.A.M.B sales had expanded from $40 million in 2005 to a predicted $90 million in 2006.Greenberg, Julee [http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-151442380.html "Gwen Stefani keeps close tabs on L.A.M.B.(Company overview)"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020122556/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-151442380.html |date=2012-10-20 }} Retrieved September 29, 2007 In March 2008, it was reported the line reached sales of $100 million.{{cite web | last=Reddy | first=Sameer | title=Fashion: Celebrity Luxury Brands | website=Newsweek | date=2008-03-08 | url=https://www.newsweek.com/fashion-celebrity-luxury-brands-84127 | access-date=2023-01-09}} According to a [[Nordstrom]] spokesperson, the debut of L.A.M.B.'s watch line was the store's most successful watch launch ever. The brand's designs have appeared in ''[[W (magazine)|W]]'', ''[[Marie Claire]]'', ''[[Elle (magazine)|Elle]]'', ''[[Lucky (magazine)|Lucky]]'' and ''[[InStyle]]''.Critchell, Samantha [http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/living/2002456156_gwenstefani30.html "Gwen Stefani: just a girl with a new fashion line"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080602160344/http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/living/2002456156_gwenstefani30.html |date=June 2, 2008}} ''Seattle Times'' Retrieved October 13, 2007 ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} {{good article}} {{Gwen Stefani}} [[Category:Clothing brands of the United States]] [[Category:Gwen Stefani]] [[Category:2000s fashion]] [[sv:L.A.M.B.]]
